_comment: What was actually exercised before handoff. Do not mark true without doing it (docs/06). Everything marked true below was run against `next start` on the production build, in a real browser, not read off the source. This pass is an independent QA re-verification, done against a freshly built `.next` and a freshly started `next start` process (see qaVerification2026-09-06 note on why that freshness check mattered), not a re-read of the prior report's claims.

howEachWasChecked.qaVerification2026-09-06: Independent re-verification pass, chrome-devtools MCP against `npx next start`. First gotcha, recorded per CLAUDE.md's 'verify against the filesystem and the build output' rule: `next start -p 3200` was already running from a prior session BEFORE this pass's `npm run build`, so the browser was loading HTML that referenced CSS/JS chunk hashes from an OLD `.next` build while the files on disk were the NEW build's (confirmed by diffing the HTML's referenced hashes against `.next/BUILD_ID` and `.next/static/css/*` on disk, and by fetching one of the referenced chunks and getting back an unrelated Pages-Router app's 400 error page). That server, and half a dozen other zombie `next start` processes from earlier sessions on other ports, were left running against the same `web/.next` directory. Rather than kill processes outside this task's permissions, every check below was re-run against a brand-new `next start -p 3250`, with its served HTML's CSS hashes confirmed to match the hashes actually present in `.next/static/css` on disk before any other testing began. Anyone re-running this suite should start their own server after their own build and verify the same way, not trust a `next start` that predates their build.
howEachWasChecked.buildPasses: npm run build, exit 0. Route / is 8.12 kB, 164 kB first load JS. Three and R3F are in the dynamic HeroScene chunk, not the first load.
howEachWasChecked.lintPasses: npm run lint, exit 0. eslint 9 flat config on next/core-web-vitals plus next/typescript, then scripts/guardrails.sh. Re-run this pass, not carried over.
howEachWasChecked.typecheckPasses: npx tsc --noEmit, no output, exit 0. Re-run this pass.
howEachWasChecked.guardrailsProvenToFail: Carried over from the implementer's pass (not re-run destructively this session): appending a literal hex to a CSS module and a real U+2014 to content/landing.ts both failed the script (exit 1), both reverted cleanly. Re-confirmed only that the script still exits 0 on the untouched tree and does not silently no-op.
howEachWasChecked.heroCanvasGPU: Chromium via chrome-devtools MCP against a freshly started next start (see qaVerification2026-09-06). <canvas> mounts inside the hero, WebGL context present, frame loop runs (screenshots differ frame to frame from grain/glyph motion). This checks that the canvas renders at all, not that every shader term is correct - see heroDuotoneToColorMix.
howEachWasChecked.heroFallbackNoWebGL: n/a per owner direction 2026-09-06 (DESIGN.md v3.3 assumes WebGL; no-WebGL path is not a requirement). Not tested this pass.
howEachWasChecked.reducedMotionPath: n/a per owner direction 2026-09-06: no prefers-reduced-motion variant exists anywhere in this codebase, on purpose (DESIGN.md, "Motion is not optional"). Confirmed no matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion...)') read anywhere in web/components or web/app.
howEachWasChecked.heroDuotoneToColorMix: FAILS. DESIGN.md and components/hero/HeroScene.tsx both specify the hero photo lifts from duotone to full colour as scroll progress crosses uMix = smoothstep(progress, 0.6, 0.69). Scrolled the pin with real WheelEvents dispatched at window (consumed by Lenis, confirmed by window.scrollY tracking the target and settling), screenshotted at scrollY 0 (progress 0), ~924 (progress ~0.68), ~1270 (progress ~0.94) and ~1331 (progress ~0.99, essentially the last frame before the pin releases). All four screenshots are visually indistinguishable duotone red - the photo never lifts to colour at any point up to the end of the pin. Cross-checked that scroll progress itself WAS being tracked correctly over this same range: the nav's transparent-to-solid switch, which is driven by the same ScrollTrigger instance reaching progress 1 (Hero.tsx onLeave/onToggle), fired exactly where expected (false at scrollY 1283, true at scrollY 1367), which rules out the wheel-scroll harness as the cause and points at the uMix/shader path specifically (components/hero/HeroScene.tsx:66, components/hero/heroShader.ts outCol = mix(duo, col, uMix)). Screenshots: 04b-hero-y924-settled.png, 05-hero-y1270.png, 06-hero-y1331-nearpinend.png, compare against 01-above-fold-1440.png. | FIXED after this pass and re-verified in pixels. Root cause: @react-three/fiber v9 clones the uniforms prop object when it constructs a ShaderMaterial (v8 shared the reference), so HeroScene's useFrame was mutating a detached object while the GPU material kept its frozen clone at uMix 0; confirmed at runtime with material.uniforms !== memo object and material uMix stuck at 0 while the memo object read 1. Fix: useFrame now writes to the material's own uniforms via a ref (HeroScene.tsx). Verified against the rebuilt production bundle by driving real wheel events in headless Chrome and measuring pixels in the frame: mean green/red ratio of the hero region goes 0.47 (duotone maroon, low progress) to 0.98 (full colour, high progress), and the copy block finishes its fade (opacity 0, visibility hidden). Screenshots fix-hero-low.png / fix-hero-high.png.
howEachWasChecked.serverRenderedFinalState: Fresh curl of the newly started production server (see qaVerification2026-09-06), 52629 bytes, parsed for content: hero photo srcset and alt, hero lede, mission headline, all six rotator phrases, the pull quote ('Every board seat is a student one.'), both spec-sheet labels, the marginalia line ('we meant it about the snacks.'), and all eight puzzle tiles in solved reading order (You / have / a / place / in / this / room / ✳) confirmed via their data-index-free aria-label attributes in the raw HTML, before any client JS runs.
howEachWasChecked.keyboardOnlyNavigation: Tab from the top of the page through the brand link, all seven primary nav links and the nav Join pill, confirming a visible gold 2px outline (rgb(255,204,51), 2px offset) at every stop via getComputedStyle. Spot-checked the same outline on: a puzzle tile, the newsletter form input, and one of FloatingCards' visually-hidden (1x1px clip) a11y-list buttons - which, per FloatingCards.module.css .a11yList:focus-within, becomes a visible on-screen list the moment any of its buttons is focused, so a sighted keyboard user is never operating something invisible. Pressed Enter on a focused gallery button: lightbox opened (FloatingCards_lightbox, focus moved into the panel). Pressed Escape: lightbox closed and focus returned exactly to the trigger button. On the puzzle: focused a tile and pressed an arrow key, board's onKeyDown handled it and focus stayed on the same logical tile (React key = word index, not DOM position). On mobile viewport (390x844): opened the [ Menu ] sheet by click, confirmed all 7 links + pill + socials render, pressed Escape, sheet closed and focus returned to the [ Menu ] button. Not a literal single continuous Tab sweep of every one of the ~50 interactive elements on the page; nav/pill were done as a real sequential Tab walk, deeper elements were spot-checked by focusing them directly (script .focus(), which Chromium treats as keyboard-modality for :focus-visible) plus real Enter/Escape/Arrow key presses.
howEachWasChecked.screenReaderHeroName:
Not run through NVDA or VoiceOver (none available in this environment). Verified the accessible-name computation directly: the hero

contains a `sr-only` span with the literal wordmark text plus a sibling `aria-hidden="true"` span holding TextRoll's per-character animated markup, so assistive tech reads exactly "ColorStack UMN" once, never the per-letter spans. Confirmed via Chromium's accessibility tree (take_snapshot) that heading levels run h1 -> h2 (mission) -> h2 (what we do) -> h3 x4 (the four programs) -> h2 (rose) -> h2 (in the room) -> h2 (get in touch), no skipped levels. Hero alt is the real photo description, not empty or generic. The gallery's WebGL canvas sits inside a `[class*=FloatingCards_stage]` wrapper carrying aria-hidden="true"; the accessible button list for the same 15 photos lives outside that wrapper and appeared correctly in the accessibility tree.
howEachWasChecked.puzzleSolvableFromShuffle: Automated: clicked Shuffle, then repeatedly clicked Hint and clicked whichever tile it marked via data-mark, nothing else. Solved in 16 moves this run, finishing on 'You have a place in this room ✳' read in row-major order off the tiles' --r/--c CSS custom properties. Also confirmed via curl that the server-rendered HTML (pre-shuffle, pre-JS) has the eight tiles in solved order already.
howEachWasChecked.navTransparentToSolidBothWays: Chromium, 1440x900, driven with real wheel events dispatched at window because Lenis snaps window.scrollTo back. At the top: background rgba(0,0,0,0). Scrolled to ~2018 (well past the pin): background rgb(255,255,255), solid class present. Scrolled back to 0: background rgba(0,0,0,0) again, solid class gone. Both directions confirmed in one script this pass.
howEachWasChecked.heroPhotoTouchesTopEdge: Hero bounding rect at 1440x900: top 0, matches viewport height. At 390x844: document.documentElement.scrollWidth stayed 390 (no horizontal overflow) at scrollY 0 and while stepping through the pin (200 through 1000 in wheel increments).
howEachWasChecked.typeScaleAtMostSixSizes: Re-verified against the fresh build's CSS: grepped every .next/static/css/*.css for font-size declarations. Six distinct var(--text-*) tokens in use (mono, body, h2, h3, lede, hero); their literal values are clamp(46px,10.5vw,132px), 40px, 22px, 20px, 17px, 11px, same six as the prior pass.
howEachWasChecked.lcpMobileMs: Chrome DevTools performance trace (performance_start_trace/stop_trace) at 390x844 DPR 2 with mobile emulation, Slow 4G network throttling and 4x CPU throttling, against the freshly started server (not an isolated cold-cache browser context this time, so treat as a hot-ish re-check rather than a strict replication of the prior cold-cache method). LCP 1009ms, TTFB 4ms, render delay 1005ms, comfortably under the 2000ms budget CLAUDE.md sets for this page.
howEachWasChecked.definitionOfDoneSweep:
Fresh curl + live DOM query against the new build. Zero matches for 'Fig.', visible 'Caption' labels, data-tag or data-cue anywhere (the one regex hit on 'caption' was the CSS module class name FloatingCards_caption, which is the intentional hover-caption feature, not an editorial caption). Mono font-family confined to exactly: the [ Menu ] bracket, the six-item 01-06 gutter index (data-index attributes read 01,02,03,04,05,06, contiguous, nothing else), the two spec-sheet
labels, and the footer (headings, links, copy-email button, legal line). No 'Voices'/'voices' substring anywhere in rendered HTML. Rose 'Who we show up for' section: background rgb(198,136,127) (--rose), zero / descendants, heading and body text both rgb(31,26,23) (--ink, the accepted WCAG AA deviation from DESIGN.md's white). Page background (html element) is white; the only two non-white, non-hero, non-rose backgrounds found are both rgb(251,245,236) (--cream), on the pull-quote band and the stat/spec band, matching 'cream only on pull-quote band and spec sheet'.
howEachWasChecked.galleryRotationAndHoverCaption: Two screenshots of the FloatingCards gallery ~1.2s apart at the same scroll position show different photos and rotation angles in most grid cells, confirming the render loop is actually animating rather than static. Dispatched pointerover/pointermove PointerEvents at a card's exact on-screen position (read from a screenshot taken immediately before); the under-canvas caption paragraph updated to that card's exact alt text ('Students at round tables with laptops during the Ideathon, a countdown timer on the screen at the front of the room' for the Ideathon-room card). Screenshots: 10-gallery-t0.png, 11-gallery-t1.png, 13-gallery-hover-caption.png.
howEachWasChecked.floatingCardsKeyboardLightbox: Covered under keyboardOnlyNavigation above; restated here because it was explicitly called out. Enter on a focused a11y-list button opens the lightbox with a visible gold border and the same alt text as a caption; Escape closes it and returns focus to the exact trigger button. Screenshot: 08-lightbox-open.png.
howEachWasChecked.mobileMenuSheet: 390x844 with mobile+touch emulation. [ MENU ] bracket visible top-right of the transparent-over-hero nav. Clicked it: full-screen white sheet with brand, [ CLOSE ] bracket, all 7 primary links, the gold Join pill and both socials. Escape closes it and returns focus to the [ Menu ] button. Screenshots: 14-mobile-hero.png, 16-mobile-menu-open.png.
howEachWasChecked.mobileGalleryReducedCount: lib/components/whimsy/FloatingCards.tsx slices the photo list to 8 on mobile (matchMedia max-width:767px) versus 16 on desktop, in a 2-column grid instead of 4. Confirmed visually at 390x844: 8 cards on screen. Screenshot: 15-mobile-gallery.png. The accessible a11y-list still exposes all 15 photos at both breakpoints, which is correct - the reduction is a rendering-cost/visual-density decision, not an access one.
howEachWasChecked.mobileNoHorizontalOverflow: document.documentElement.scrollWidth === clientWidth === 390 at rest and at six scroll positions through the hero pin (0 through 1000 in wheel-driven steps, landing scrollY up to 2862).
howEachWasChecked.consoleCleanAfterInteraction: list_console_messages after the full interaction pass (hero scrub, puzzle solve, lightbox open/close, gallery hover, mobile menu open/close): only 'Failed to load resource: 404' entries, consistent with the documented gaps (no favicon, unbuilt nav routes prefetching). No JavaScript errors, no React warnings, no shader/WebGL errors.

notDoneAndWhy.mobileSafariPin: No Apple device available here. ScrollTrigger pins plus Lenis on iOS Safari is the classic place this breaks.
notDoneAndWhy.lighthouseMobilePerformance: The Lighthouse *performance category score* (0-100) still is not run: the only Lighthouse tool available this session (chrome-devtools MCP's lighthouse_audit) explicitly excludes the performance category and only covers accessibility/best-practices/SEO/agentic-browsing. Core Web Vitals were re-measured directly via a DevTools performance trace instead (see lcpMobileMs/clsMobile), which is a real measurement of LCP and CLS, just not the weighted 0-100 Lighthouse performance score.
notDoneAndWhy.screenReaderHeroName_caveat: Re-verified this pass via the accessible-name computation and Chromium's own accessibility tree, which is what NVDA/VoiceOver ultimately read from, but the literal software has still not been run against the page. Marked true on the strength of the DOM/AX-tree evidence; flag for a real AT pass before launch if that distinction matters.

knownGaps: Nav routes /about /programs /events /newsletter /opportunities /resources /wunderbar /contact /sponsor /privacy all 404. Landing only, as briefed. They appear as prefetch 404s in the console.
Voices and the community PhotoRoll were deleted as the carousel/slider components. The rose section has no image slot now rather than a still stand-in.

components/ui/SideNav.tsx, components/editorial/MetaRow.tsx and MetaSidebar.tsx, and components/motion/ZoomImage.tsx are carried from the handoff and compile, but nothing on this page uses them. Their CSS was brought onto the type scale anyway so it cannot drift back in.

public/images/colorstack-umn-mark-192.webp is 192px on its longest side and was KEPT despite the under-1200px deletion rule. It is the chapter mark, rendered at 24px in the nav and 32px in the footer, and DESIGN.md requires both. Deleting it would remove the logo from the site. Flagged rather than done silently.
RESOLVED: the duotone-to-colour bug found this pass (R3F v9 uniforms clone) is fixed and pixel-verified; see howEachWasChecked.heroDuotoneToColorMix.
notes: No reduced-motion path exists and none is reported on: DESIGN.md, "Motion is not optional", owner-confirmed 2026-09-06 that no variant exists on purpose. The hero keeps a WebGL guard and an error boundary, which DESIGN.md permits but does not require (no-WebGL path is explicitly not a requirement per owner direction, not tested this pass). One gradient exists on the whole site, the hero legibility scrim, authorised for contrast. The rose band carries ink text rather than the white DESIGN.md originally asked for: white on #C6887F measures 2.9:1 and fails WCAG AA, ink measures 5.9:1 and passes; this is a DESIGN.md-documented, owner-accepted deviation, re-confirmed this pass (background rgb(198,136,127), text rgb(31,26,23), zero image/canvas descendants - the section is genuinely text-only). Hinted puzzle tile: renders ink background / paper text (RoomPuzzle.module.css .tile[data-mark]), not gold. The CSS comment says this is deliberate: DESIGN.md marks the hint gold, but the owner's colour rule confines gold to the pill, the mission underline and the focus ring, so the hinted tile inverts to ink instead. Recorded as a flagged, source-documented deviation, not a bug. Nav item count: DESIGN.md's own checklist phrase "all eight nav items" is satisfied by 7 named links (About, Programs, Events, Newsletter, Opportunities, Resources, Wunderbar) plus the gold Join the List pill = 8 clickable items in the header; this is not a shortfall, just worth spelling out since "eight nav items" reads ambiguously against a 7-item list. The one real finding from this pass is heroDuotoneToColorMix (see knownGaps) - everything else exercised this session passed, including a fresh Core Web Vitals measurement (LCP 1009ms / CLS 0.00, comfortably under budget) and a full Lighthouse a11y/best-practices/SEO/agentic sweep at 100/100/100/100.
